aspects.says: When a condition is joined to a pattern with &&, an object of that type that fails the condition goes on to the next branch, and in an if chain the first matching pattern wins, so a supertype tested first takes its subtypes.
basis: section:A Condition Joined with && Sends a Matching Object That Fails It to the Next Branch

aspects.says: Where a pattern variable is out of scope, a field of the same name is used without any error, so a guard that falls through reads the field.
basis: section:Out of Its Scope, a Pattern Variable's Name Means the Field
section:Spot the Problem: A Guard That Logs Instead of Returning

aspects.says: A pattern variable is an ordinary local: reassignable unless declared final, and once reassigned a lambda can't capture it; a local of the same name is a compile error.
basis: section:A Pattern Variable Exists Only Where the Match Is Certain

aspects.says: A pattern variable is in scope only where the test is known to be true: after &&, in the true branch of ?:, in the else of a negated test, and after a statement that can't finish while the test is false; not after || or &, and not after a negated if that falls through.
basis: section:A Pattern Variable Exists Only Where the Match Is Certain

aspects.says: Since Java 21 a pattern whose type the declared type already guarantees compiles, and instanceof is still false for null, so it acts as a null check that binds.
basis: section:Since Java 21 a Pattern of the Declared Type Compiles, and It Is Still False for null
